headline: LYNAS TARGETS BRAZIL FOR NEXT RARE EARTH OXIDE PLANT — GOVERNMENT BACKING COULD MAKE IT LARGEST NON-CHINA NdPr FACILITY OUTSIDE ASIA
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths presented plans on October 12 for a rare earth oxide separation plant in Minas Gerais, Brazil, with Brazil's mines minister indicating the government is considering state backing. If funded and built, the facility could become one of the largest rare earth processing plants outside China, targeting neodymium-praseodymium oxide critical for EV and defence permanent magnets — a significant step toward Western supply chain diversification.

headline: MAIDEN URANIUM RESOURCE IN ARGENTINA: JAGUAR URANIUM ESTABLISHES LAGUNA SALADA AS SOUTH AMERICAN DEVELOPMENT PLAY
snippet: Jaguar Uranium announced on October 13 its maiden mineral resource estimate for the Laguna Salada uranium-vanadium project in Chubut Province, Argentina — effective October 5, 2026. The first-ever resource for the project gives investors a quantified view of the deposit's scale at a time when long-term uranium contract prices are at 18-year highs above $97 per pound and utility re-contracting is accelerating.

headline: RARE EARTH RUSH GOES ROYAL: MALAYSIA'S KING BUYS 2.25% STAKE IN MINING FIRM EXPANDING INTO RARE EARTHS
snippet: Malaysia's Yang di-Pertuan Agong acquired a 2.25% stake in Singapore-listed Southern Alliance Mining on October 13 — a company expanding its rare earth operations including a project in Johor, the king's home state. The royal investment signals institutional alignment with the global critical minerals race and underscores Southeast Asia's push to develop domestic rare earth supply chains outside Chinese control.

headline: LITHIUM CRASHES TO 5-MONTH LOW AS MINE RESTARTS PILE ON — 2027 OVERSUPPLY FEAR OVERRIDES NEAR-TERM EV DEMAND
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices slid to a five-month low, with spot falling to approximately 115,400 yuan per tonne on October 12, as restarting mine supply stoked fears of a significant 2027 production surplus. The decline pressures junior lithium developers whose project economics are sensitive to spot pricing, even as cathode producers maintain near-term demand is structurally intact heading into the fourth quarter EV sales push.

headline: CATL MINE SHUTDOWN THREATENS TO FLIP LITHIUM FROM GLUT TO DEFICIT — SUPPLY SHOCK COUNTER-NARRATIVE EMERGES
snippet: A production shutdown at a CATL-linked mine threatens to introduce a supply-side shock that most bearish lithium forecasts had not modelled, potentially reversing the anticipated 2027 oversupply narrative. The development is a counterpoint to this week's price rout and illustrates how quickly market dynamics can shift when a dominant battery materials processor loses captive supply.

headline: GOLD MINERS FACE 23% MARGIN SQUEEZE AS SPOT FALLS FROM $5,589 PEAK — UNHEDGED PRODUCERS HIT HARDEST IN Q4
snippet: An October 2026 analysis models gold mining margins at roughly 23% below their Q1 2026 peak, when the average realized price reached approximately $4,873 per ounce — spot has since corrected to around $4,165 while all-in sustaining costs have remained elevated. The squeeze hits unhedged producers hardest and frames the October 27–28 Federal Reserve policy decision as the key near-term macro catalyst that could reprice the sector one way or another.

headline: ARKLE RESOURCES CONFIRMS URANIUM DISCOVERY AT ULG — MAIDEN DRILLING FINDS URANIUM WITH RARE EARTH CO-ENRICHMENT
snippet: Arkle Resources' maiden drilling program has confirmed a uranium discovery at its ULG project, with the company noting that follow-up work will also investigate how uranium and rare earth enrichment correlate within the system. The dual-commodity potential adds a rare earths optionality angle on top of the primary uranium thesis at a moment when both critical minerals are attracting heightened investor interest.

headline: ELECTRA BATTERY SEALS COBALT REFINERY TERM SHEET WITH WMC — CANADIAN CRITICAL MINERAL PROCESSING TAKES SHAPE
snippet: Electra Battery Materials (TSX: ELBM) signed a strategic term sheet with WMC on October 13 for support of its cobalt refinery in Ontario, Canada — one of the few battery-grade cobalt processing facilities being developed outside Asia. The deal represents incremental progress toward a fully domestic North American battery supply chain at a time when Western governments are actively de-risking critical mineral processing from Chinese supply chains.
